title: Dave Canales: 'The energy was right' coming out of the bye week | Carolina Panthers
text: Yeah, what a day. Um, just a I I think one of the coolest parts about today, first of all, the weather is beautiful. It was perfect outside, but then um just the joy, the gratitude coming out of guys like Taylor Motton, uh Turk Wharton back at practice, uh Trevor, you know, these guys that have been waiting to get back and be with their teammates on the grass. And uh you could just feel that. You could feel the excitement from them in the reps. Um, you know, Trevor taking his returns, getting up the field, finishing way too long on stuff, just feeling good running, uh, being out there with his teammates. And so, it's infectious. Um, the guys are fresh, you know, coming off this this rest that we've had. Um, it was a spirited practice. It was a great time and, uh, wasn't the cleanest. We got stuff to clean up for sure. Um, but the energy was right and the spirit of it was right. And I just love leaning into those moments. Um, when you get to just kind of look around and enjoy it. And, uh, of course, nobody could break the team down today other than Taylor Motton. So, you know, he got out there and the guys were excited about it. So, um, great day. >> David, why did you have practice today and have an off day on Wednesday? >> Yeah. So, um, you know, just friends around the league. Um, different ways to do things coming off of a buy. This is also something teams do uh going into the season in the first week. We didn't do it uh this year. Um, but when we think about it, you're getting you have a little bit of a break. So, yesterday we had, you know, some some movement, some workout stuff. uh shorter meetings, get the coaches back in in there to get the game plan done. Then getting out there on Tuesday earlier in the week, you get a chance to really knock the rust off, you know, and they haven't done football while while the guys had had opportunities, uh to work out. I think one of the days we had about 35 or 36 guys here, um last week on the by-week, uh which I haven't really been a part of that, so the guys enjoy being here. But um anyway, getting that first that first practice in on Tuesday, the high intensities, we patted up. It was a physical day. Giving him a day to recover tomorrow. Um and then being able to come back going Thursday, Friday, Saturday all the way through our normal routine. Just thought it it gives us an opportunity to really get after it and then to just give a little break knowing Thursday is going to be a high mileage day as as well to take advantage of the rest and take advantage of uh guys getting a little bit of juice in their legs. >> Dave, um last week or week four, uh Kim Jackson had a knee injury, but you guys have designated him on IR with a shoulder injury. what happened within that time frame. >> Yeah, he's just a little bit banged up. Um, and you know, these are these are all things that of course we have to be led by the player. Um, and the symptoms and and how he's feeling about being out there practicing, you know, and he hasn't been active. Um, but we play we practice physically, you know, and so these are the things that, you know, kind of kept popping up and, you know, we made a decision to, uh, put him on IR right now um to, uh, to address this address some of the issues he has going on. Um, the surgery will be in his shoulder. Um, so the knee is is uh non-surgical, just a rehab thing, but um the the shoulder was, you know, significant enough to be repaired. Thought we could get him focused on that part and then uh and then bring him back to us, you know, um after his recovery. >> Dave, of the three guys coming off IR, Turk and Taylor, and Trevor, um do you expect any of them to be ready for Sunday or is it going to take is it, you know, is it take couple >> weeks? Well, we'll give the full injury report uh tomorrow. What I will say is they all look pretty good today. We have to see how they respond to today's, you know, physical practice. And um they all got a good significant amount of reps. That was the plan. Um as you can imagine, you know, there's a there's a ramp up and training part of it getting their body right. They're in great shape. Football shape's different and this is a collision sport, you know, not a contact sport. So wanted to see how their bodies respond uh to a physical padded practice before we make any decisions. >> Do you say whether Cam would be season ending shoulder? >> Yeah, he's not a designation. So it'll be season ending rehab and then uh um but he the expectation is that he'll be around us and he'll continue to grow with this group uh be involved with the meetings and um and be connected just like a lot of our guys have been. >> Coach, a quick question on Wheatley. uh looking back at his scouting report and he listed his weaknesses as as uh inconsistent with tackles, his footwork and coverage and getting beat on on double moves. In the six months that he's been with the program, how has he refined those skills to put forth a all rookie type season so far? >> I haven't seen any of those things show up for for Zigg. Um he's been a fantastic tackler in the open field. Um he's learning, I will say that. um while while he's been in the right positions for the most part, you know, I think the next step for Zigg is to be able to evaluate things so that he can so we can all see how good his hands are. Um that's one thing I think that I've seen in practice throughout camp. Um he's got magnificent hands and so the next part of it making those plays is being able to take his opportunities when they come to him down the field. >> Receiver, right? >> Yeah, he's he's he's a special talent and he just has a real sense of of just playing football. >> Any chance on using him on special teams as as a receiver? Maybe I don't know for for we have a bunch of different roles for for the guys that have to be ready to play. Um but while guys are focusing for for Zigg for example, you know, while he's focusing on helping on the defensive side, you know, there are other guys that are helping us. Of course, we have Isaiah Simmons, you know, one of our safeties who's a phenomenal special teams player. And so they he kind of plays some of those roles. >> Dave, you mentioned Teemo breaking down the team with what he means to this place and all these people. What was that moment out there like? And and could you see kind of the way people responded to him today? >> Yeah, they respond to him like a fun uncle. Um, you know, he's and and he accepts and embraces that role. That's something he did well in college. Is it more so like tapping into something he has a good grasp on or was it kind of just situational with with how the Lions played their defense. >> Yeah, we've been running them for I mean really for two and a half years they were presenting opportunities so they really came to life um where you can keep going back to them based on the space that was available. Um, so it wasn't really an emphasis that we said, "Hey, this week guys, we're really gonna," it's always been a part of what we've done. Um, you know, throwing different combinations on some of our runs, giving him the option to throw the ball, you know, inseams to the flat, different things like that. Um, but, you know, told Brad stomp the puddle out so there's no water left, you know, and it's just, um, it's a fun part when those things kind of come alive >> because of the way Chuba runs. I mean, he doesn't you're not losing a lot of yardage with him. Why why is he a really good asset for those RPOS's because of how it affects the defender? >> Yeah, his downhill nature. Um and like one of the things I learned way back, you know, way back when I was studying Urban Meyer, you know, when he was at Utah and it was like they would tell the backs replace the space and if the backer plays the the route concept, the running back go get the void that they left, you know, and so um those principles fit with what how Chuba runs. Um he's aggressive, he's downhill decisive, so it's a good combo. >> What has it been like to see Bryce get all this attention? You caught him on the Manning cast last night and then conversely, what do you notice about him as he kind of deals with that external attention when he's here? >> Honestly, I haven't really, you know, leaned into listening to all that. Um this is a it's timely and this this type of attention is earned by working hard every day. um by trying to find out how good you can be, mastering different parts of your game. Um his natural growth and progression, just continues to take strides every week as he learns new things about certain defenses, as he learns new things about his guys, about our players. And um this is right, this is right on par. Um the goal is to just be focused on the Eagles, on this practice. And that's what I've seen from Bryce. um he hasn't changed regardless of circumstances, whether it be in a positive way this way or whether it been in a negative way at different times. You know, the nature of the position, my position, you have to be able to to hear those things, see those things. And the bottom line is what matters is our preparation for today. Can we get back to our ball? Can we take the next step as a team? >> How did look out there? And uh you know, >> he looked great. Yeah, Coker looked great. Um he had a really nice day today. Uh we'll see how he responds. Again, this is a this is a high load for him practice-wise coming off of uh the quad and the ankle. So, um and again, we'll give specifics on the questionable, doubtful, all that thing. Um as as we could go in tomorrow, >> a couple more do a couple more. >> Without knowing when Turk might be activated again, how does he kind of complement the other people you have in that front? Yeah, he's he's just built different, you know, um a little bit leaner up top, you know, and uh the suddenness at the line of scrimmage, the leverage that he plays with. Um he's a different type of player than Derek, than Bobby, than Lee Hunter, you know, and um so he just he adds a lot of juice. Um plays plays with his hair on fire and uh really disruptive, you know, whether it's in the run game or the pass game. >> Dave, three months ago, Darren Waller wasn't on the Panthers roster. Um, now five weeks into the season, he's third in the team in, I believe, receiving yards and tied for the team leading receiving touchdowns. How has his uh arrival kind of like what were you expecting from him when he first came to the team? And how has have those expectations perhaps been exceeded? >> Yeah. Um, >> really, I think there's still more. Um, I think there's still, you know, different ways to utilize his talents. He creates interesting matchups for us um inside the box against linebackers and safeties. Um teams that keep the corners opposite, you know, uh the corners don't realize how fast he is when he's running across the field. And he's made quite a few receptions that way, you know, where um doesn't look like he's moving fast. It's just that he's 66, you know, and and he's still, you know, upwards of 19 plus miles per hour in the route. And so, um, my dream, my vision was, you know, when Dan brought the possibility of having Darren here, I was like, "Yes, absolutely. Can we make that happen?" Just knowing that he could create horizontal and vertical stretch in the pass game. Um, and then also just get favorable looks when teams want to play nickel defense to 12 personnel when you have two tight ends out there. That's an advantage for us in the run game. So, um, all those things are are really starting to, uh, materialize for us. um and he just when when they have to regard that person, all of a sudden it creates more space for the other guys as well. So, um I'm I'm really pleased with where we're at right now and I know that there's still more we can do. >> David, um were you able to watch the Eagles Jaguars game live and just for you specifically, is there any advantage? I know you want to focus on the actual game film, that All 22, but is there an advantage to watching something live and then going back to it with your study? >> Yeah, that's that's part of my process weekly. Um, I usually start off with the TV copy of the team that we're playing that week. Um, and the reason I like that is because, uh, I think the commentators do such a great job of painting a picture of the story. Um, and, uh, this guy's just coming back from this or that or this guy is having a historic run, you know, and they they uh, they let you know more specifics than you would just pick up from studying the all 22 or just looking at a normal stat sheet. there's stories within the story and I don't know how much that affects the decisions that we make but it does give me a sense of who we're playing not just from an X's and O's standpoint but where are they at you know and you see the faces and you see the zoomed in face of the coach you see the zoomed in face of the quarterback or the you know defensive player and um and it gives you a sense for you know how comfortable they feel you know is there is there pressure here is there a level of confidence here um so that you get this just a live just human kind of feel to Thank you very much. >> Okay. Thank you. [music] >> [music]

title: Bills Postgame Live: Bills Monday Night Football Win over LA | Week Five
text: Mhm. >> Mhm. >> Bills-Rams took a couple years off of our lives. Tyler Bass hits a 45-yard game-winning field goal in overtime. Bills win it 37-34. Welcome in to Bills Postgame Live. He's Bills legend George Wilson. I'm Maddy Glab. Overtime starts and chaos ensues, George. Bills get the ball first. A costly James Cook fumble gives the ball back to the Rams. First score wins it. Rams drive down the field to set up a 48-yard field goal attempt. Outside linebacker Greg Rousseau blocks it. Bills get the ball back. Josh Allen scrambles for over 30 yards, which sets up a Tyler Bass game-winning 45-yard field goal. The Bills didn't give up to the very end of it, and that would That's what allowed Buffalo to get the victory. >> Yeah, that's the key tonight. You know, they normally say it's a 60-minute game. Tonight, it took a little bit more, but that's why you have to focus on the next play. If you think about the last play, you get down, you start questioning how the game's going to end. You got to stay focused. You got to stay in the moment. The Bills as a team, especially as a defense, did that tonight. Defense went out there after the fumble, didn't give up the big play. They moved the ball The Rams moved the ball down the field, and when it came down to the kick, Greg Rousseau stepped up like he's done all season, made a big play to give the Bills offense one more opportunity. >> When you're on field goal unit, on field goal block, it is so hard to step through that line and get into a place where you have your hand up to block the field goal. George, what has to happen to put Greg Rousseau in that type of opportunity? >> They created some separation between the linemen right there. It's just a little bit of a crack. It's all you need to be able to step through. The key is to try to get your feet on the offensive side of the line of scrimmage on those kicks. Greg was able to do that, reach out his long arms, got his hand on the football, and all of Bills Mafia rejoiced when their ball fell just short of the goalpost. >> Greg Rousseau, what a hot start to the season he's had. Now he's making plays on special teams. Bills get the ball back thanks to Greg Rousseau blocking that field goal. Josh Allen scrambles for over 30 yards. It sets up a Tyler Bass 45-yard field goal attempt. Second and 10, 2 minutes left on the clock. Bills head coach Joe Brady says Tyler Bass go for it right here. What does that say about Brady? >> That say he has all the confidence in the world in his kicker Tyler Bass. He stepped up had two more downs or at least one more down that he could have ran another play, got in a little closer, ran some more time on the clock just in case the field goal missed. But he had all the confidence in the world. Tyler steps up, great operation, snap, hold, kick. Game winning field goal in overtime sends the Bills to four and one. >> Bills are now four and one on the season. You are correct. They have a two game stand on the west coast and what a way to go in to that two week stand that you have across the country with a big victory on Monday night football. Josh Allen on the podium speaking to media right now. Let's hear from QB1. >> Every play? >> Curious the way that game ended though with the with the missed field goal. I mean you got to be standing there thinking it's probably not good at that point, right? >> I mean, again, it's it's football. You can be down and out uh one play, the next play you're on top of the world and again that's just how it rolled for us today. Um a lot of things to clean up. Early on just didn't feel like I was in a rhythm. Wasn't taking some of the underneath stuff. Um you know, fighting mechanically some stuff right now that I'm working on. Um but I felt like in that second half I got into a rhythm. Um and guys made some plays. I mean Khalil in that that first catch in the overtime. Um it's awesome stuff. Um got to be better in the pass game. We we know that. We understand that. But we'll take a win no matter what. >> At what point did you kind of decide your legs had to be the main thing today? >> I mean this is kind of how the way the game rolled. Um it's a really good secondary. It's a really good defense. Um didn't want to shout out Bates for coming in at right tackle when Spencer went down. Uh he stepped in and I mean couldn't tell you he he was out there which is always was good sign. So um our guys blocked well, we ran the ball well. Obviously, we want to hold on to the football. Uh, two turnovers tonight, that's not it's not good enough. Um, so we got got some stuff to clean up. >> What happened on the final drive of the first half? It seemed like there was communication issue where you guys lost some time on the clock there. >> Yeah, just uh, got to be better in our operation, it starts with me, so um, we'll look at the film and find a way to get better. >> What did you say to James after the after the fumble in overtime? >> Um, just you you don't got to say nothing to him. He he's a competitor, he knows, um, you know, but got another opportunity, you know, that's the beautiful thing about football. Um, you got another drive, you got another game. So, that's that's all you can do is keep moving forward. >> What's being said or done on the sideline during that Rams drive in overtime where you guys crossing your fingers? What are you doing? >> Uh, absolutely crossing your fingers. You're you're hoping someone on defense or special teams to make a play. Um, and that's that's what happened. Greg Rousseau made a play. >> You know the you know the projections with these two teams and the expectations. What's it like to come in here on the road and Monday night and and get a win out of this? >> Yeah, I mean, we we have a West Coast uh, two-game stint on the West Coast. Um, you know, our goal is to to go one and oh each week. Um, we wanted to go two and oh this this West Coast trip and you can't go two and oh without getting the first one, so um, we did our our the first part of our job. We got to have a really good week on a short short week going against a, you know, really good team in the Raiders. Um, enjoy this one tonight, flush it and get on to the next. >> What is it that you're working on mechanically? >> Um, just ball position. Um, you know, it coming out of my hand, I want it to feel as good as possible in that second half. I just said, you know what, turn off the mind and and throw the dang ball and that's that's kind of what I did and felt pretty good. I don't know the splits from first half to second half, but I felt like we got into a rhythm there in the second. >> Can you elaborate on it? What like what it is about it? >> If I could, I think we wouldn't be talking about it, so. >> The decision you had second and 10 at the end there at the 40 it would have been a 40 it was a 45 yd kick. What was what did the decision to kick it then? >> It's in the range of the zero um every play and you can you know hit your head into a wall and hopefully you get yardage but you're putting the ball at risk every time you do that even with good ball security but you're you're potential penalties, potential turnovers um felt very confident about the left hash and T Basham wanted it there and you know felt like it was within his range um within his safety range and Joe made the decision to to put the ball down and kick it and and T Basham drilled one. >> We could talk about all the things that you want to clean up but to get this win against this team on the road at this point in the season coming off of last week, what does that mean? >> It's awesome. Um again we're we're we'll take them how we get them, you know, however ugly, however pretty it looks, if we score more than them, we've done our job, so yeah. >> What are your thoughts on Tyler Bass? >> Say it again. >> Your thoughts on Tyler Bass to make that kick and just to have >> I mean that's that's who T Basham is, you know, we we we trust him implicitly yeah, go out there and drill a kick to win a game, that feels pretty good. >> You had a lot of rushing yards, a lot of big ones affected the game more so it seemed with your feet than throwing. How much do you enjoy that aspect of the game? >> I listen I'm I when it's there, it's there. Um I don't want to make a living in that, I understand that. Um but I do know how much of a backbreaker that can be on a defense when you feel like you're in pretty good coverage um and the D-line you know felt like they were getting into to good spots but feeling like there were some some room to maneuver in there and um just finding ways to keep the chains moving there especially late in the game um >> When you have a game like this where you're having so many explosive runs, do you get into any kind of zone where you're seeing it differently? When you get out in space >> Not necessarily. Again, they they had a good good coverage plan. Um you know, we can clean up some details and ball placement and taking some early stuff earlier in the game like I alluded to him. Yeah, sometimes it's just kind of drop back and they open up and that's just kind of how the game went tonight. >> You have a lot of respect for Matthew. Did you watch what he was doing out there? >> Yeah, I mean I can read the stats. He had a pretty pretty good night. Um Yeah, he's a he's a stud and I said this on the broadcast. So, you know, he's my opinion he's if he's not the greatest thrower of the football, he's number two and he's an absolute stud. >> Josh, you've been you've been mindful about limiting hits this year. There was a couple times you threw the shoulder down and just just went for it. Was there like one Josh on each shoulder in in those moments? >> Uh just the flow of the game. >> Josh, what can you say about the overall play of the running back room? I mean, Cook finds the end zone a couple times, but you get explosive plays in the passing game from Ty Johnson and Raheem Mostert to just What do you think about the play of that room? >> Yeah, guys staying ready. Um I've talked about Ty for a long time just finding you know, friendly space on some of these scramble drills. Um and then Raheem Mostert staying ready and and you know, play that we just put in this last week. Um didn't have the right personnel on the field, but we went ahead and called it. Um did his job and got us down to the two-yard line. We scored and um it's just guys that again, they're not going to complain about not getting the ball and we got James Cook who's going to get majority of the rush attempts. they want to affect the game any way that they can in a positive way and they did that tonight. >> Hey Josh, I know it's do whatever you can to win the game, but obviously only four catches to receivers tonight. What kind of were they doing that kind of take that away? >> Uh they got some good DBs out there and I don't Like I said, I I didn't do a good enough job of taking some of the early stuff. I'm finding myself in a rhythm. you know, and again, that's just kind of how that we were running it so well that just kind of how it played out tonight. >> Talk a lot about how different things are when DJ's not out there. Could you feel his absence more tonight? >> Um I mean, yeah, again, we we ran the ball so well tonight. Uh it'd be hard to say any other or you know, otherwise. Um but he's a stud. We we want him out there cuz he makes our offense better. >> Thanks, George. >> Quarterback Josh Allen's legs were a weapon against the Rams. He finishes with 107 scramble yards. Allen took advantage of the open zones that he saw in the Rams defense. The Rams are a man coverage team, top 10 in the NFL. Going up against a mobile quarterback, that gives mobile quarterbacks opportunities to run and to find some extra yards on the ground. George, Josh Allen took advantage of that. >> Took full advantage of that tonight, Maddie. When you're in man coverage on defense, you don't have vision on the quarterback when he pulls the ball down to run. He took advantage of that tonight time after time after time and time again, and he kept the chains moving, kept the drives going, and was able to put the Bills offense in position to score a lot of points tonight. Exciting finish to the game, but Josh took what the defense gave him. Most of the time when you say that, it's in the it's in the throwing context, but tonight he took what the defense gave him on the ground. He saw the openings in the rush lanes, took advantage of it, got a lot of yards on the ground, and that's what you want to see with with your with your team leader and the leader of your of your offense. >> Allen finishes with 121 rushing yards on the day. His 107 scramble yards are the most by any player since 2015. Now, George, Allen was racking up those scramble yards in the first half and into the third quarter. Why didn't the Rams make a big adjustment to try to stop him? Because it continued into the fourth quarter. >> The only thing they really could have done is maybe put a man spy on them, but that takes a guy out of coverage or it takes a guy out of the rush. And so it's kind of a pick your own poison when you're going against a guy like Josh Allen. He puts you in a conundrum where you're you're between a rock and a hard place. Do you rush him? Do you drop in coverage? He's He's He's an anomaly in this league and tonight he showed that. >> It was an interesting first half out of Buffalo's offense. It was tough for Buffalo's offense to get into a rhythm, really get into their playbook. We saw only four completions for 60 passing yards out of Josh Allen in the first half. Why was it so tough to get to the air against the Rams? >> The Rams have great athletes in their secondary. You know, we we you know, didn't have DJ Moore in the lineup tonight. And so the Rams did what they do best. They play a lot of man coverage, was able to try to get some pressure on Josh with their four or five man rush. But at the end of the day, the Bills stayed ahead of schedule running the ball with Cook early in the game. Josh again, like we already talked about, staying ahead of the of the chains and staying on schedule with with getting runs himself. And so that put the Bills offense in a place where they didn't have to have a lot of third downs early on. I think in the first half they were maybe over three, but there wasn't a lot of third down situations for the Bills offense in the first half and that's because of all the success they were having on first and second down. >> And speaking of the Rams secondary, they have Troy McDiffie, one of the best cornerbacks in the NFL. He's so good at locking things down and covering. The Rams only allow 4.8 yards per pass attempt. So you figured going into this game, the Bills were going to have to find different ways to win rather than in the air. They do that early on by handing the ball to James Cook. Cook sets the run in motion early for Buffalo and you saw Buffalo really take advantage of running the football in the first half of the game. >> Yes, they definitely did that and that's the key. I mean, the Bills offense is at their best when they can run the ball, establish the run on the ground, and be able to use their play-action pass game off of that. Tonight, the Rams secondary did an exceptional job of taking away the Bills wide receivers, but the tight end stepped up, the running back stepped up. Taj Jackson, four catches for 72 yards. Raheem Mostert with a big run after the screen pass completion for 31 yards. And so, the everybody else started stepping up and making plays and that's a team win. I mean, when you look at tonight's game, it wasn't just one guy. Yes, Josh put his cape on at times to be able to make make big gains on the ground, but everybody had a moment in the game where they had to step up and make a big play. Raheem Mostert opens up the game, 70-yard run on on the opening kickoff. Taj Jackson comes in, gives us four catches, 72 yards on third-down situations, and passing situations. Secondary gets banged up. Guys coming in and out. I mean, you get Tyler Bass comes in, when Spencer Brown goes out. It's a team win, and you never know when your number's going to be called. And that's why in this league they say you're one play away. You're one play away of getting the opportunity of a lifetime, and tonight, the Bills stepped up in those moments when they had to. >> Well, Tyler Bass got the opportunity of a lifetime. A 45-yard game-winner in overtime to beat the Rams. Bass is in the locker room after the big field goal. Let's hear what he had to say. >> They might kick earlier than we were told. >> No, I again, I was just super present. Whenever coach says, "Hey, it's time." it's time. And just listen to him. >> Tyler, earlier in the game, during the game, you did miss one. You go out there. How do you put that behind you to make sure that you're ready for this one? >> Yeah, again, I I'm human, man. I make mistakes. I think I just towed it a little bit. So, I just after a miss, I just make one correction, keep it simple, push forward, and go from there. >> I know you guys like to watch when the other team's kicking, too. What was your vantage point on Greg's block? >> Um honestly, I I didn't really see it. I was just behind. I saw it and I kind of saw it get tipped and after that I just kind of locked in from the kickoff my opportunity. >> You also had a big return for today. You enabled all of your special teams. >> Yeah, yeah, yeah. We worked really hard. Jeff put a great game plan in and the guys went out there and did our jobs. >> Taylor, I know that it's kind of been a season where you you haven't had these moments or at least I don't think where you Here we are week five and you make this big kick. Is it Is the I'm not trying to put words in your mouth, but is it the season start for you today? >> Um no, no, man. The season started for me the second I got out of my surgery in um in November. That's when I kind of just put my focus forward and that's when I started, man. This has been a long time coming and just happy to to go out there and do my job and enjoy it. >> Is there some validation though? >> Um absolutely. Yeah, I mean just going out there and just seeing your routine and trusting your process and seeing things executed, man. It It's It's pretty cool. >> How much do you relish that opportunity especially after just a moment earlier you saw that guy had a chance to win. >> Yes. Um yeah, you appreciate it. You appreciate the opportunity and you just kind of try to make the most of it, man. >> How How difficult >> That's Tyler Bass who hit the game-winning field goal in overtime speaking about what that was like and he said it I just trusted my process. And it's so awesome to see a player like Bass come through in this type of moment knowing last year he did not participate in any part of the season due to a sports hernia. Took the entire season and off-season really to come back from that inner injury and to have a confidence-boosting moment like that where you can win the game for your team and he does that. text: [music] Welcome back to Lions Collective. I'm your host Jeff Freddy. Alongside me is the crew from Lions Collective. We're live every single Wednesday, Justin Rogers, Detroit Football Network, Will Birfield 97 won the ticket and Colton Paly from The Athletic. We got a lot to get into. Lions won in a dominant fashion and uh these are the shows I look forward to because we're going to talk about it today is the defense back the offense playing lights out. Let's talk about it and uh all all the story lines. We have our dog and pony show picks as well. But before we get into football because we're going to have plenty of time to do that. Uh, I did want to have uh some words for our good friend, and he's popped on the show a couple of times with me, Will, Dan Miller, who's someone, by the way, has meant a lot to Detroit sports fans, including young broadcasters like myself because we've heard him so much uh during some of the biggest moments of football. But again, condolences go out to him and his family. Obviously Dan lost his wife Cindy to cancer, but uh right now I think it's important that you know you heard Dan, you heard Jared Goff, but the entire city is behind you Dan. And uh you know he's been there for so many unforg unforgettable moments, but I just thought we spent so much time on football and talking about football, but I think today and right now is a good time to kind of reflect on uh family and what's the most important right now. So uh we love you, Dan Miller. Thank you for inspiring the next generation of broadcasters, including myself and uh the Lions Collective crew uh is with you during this time. >> Yeah, no doubt, man. That was well said, Jeff. Dan Miller is probably the most unanimously adored person in Detroit sports media. Maybe in Detroit media. Maybe in Detroit, period. There isn't a single person that would have anything but glowing things to say about Dan Miller. His wife was an absolute warrior through this two-year battle [clears throat] and then found out two years ago in the middle of that Cowboys game that his wife was in the hospital with two tumors in her brain. And he could tell based on some text interactions with her that day that something was a miss. And so at halftime he called home and he spoke with Cindy briefly. And Cindy, because he was in the middle of calling the Lions Cowboys game, didn't want to tell him what was going on. Didn't think that he should be burdened with that in the middle of his job. And he told her, and I'm not speaking out of turn here, because he has shared this with me and a few others, I'm not going back on the air until you tell me what's wrong. Until you tell me what's happening. And so he pried that news out of her. and he spent the rest of that game wearing on his heart, on his mind that his wife was going through um the most wicked thing you could ever imagine um upon anyone. And over the next two years, neither he nor Cindy ever flinched. I spend I spent a lot I consider myself lucky to spend a lot of time with Dan. And you would think that as he was going through this, everyone around him would be a rock for him. And I'm telling you guys, it was the opposite. He was a rock for everyone else. He helped uplift the people that were hurting for him. And I know in every interaction he had with people in the Lions facility, specifically Dan Campbell and Jared Goff one-on-one every week, they said the same thing. And the the outreach for Dan that we all heard and saw from Dan and Jared on Sunday after the game was so sincere and so heartfelt because of that. And um you know I had a chance to talk with Dan Campbell yesterday interviewing him for Lions Review which is a segment that usually Dan Miller sits down with him for. But of course Dan's been out for the past week or so. And I I told Dan how much we all appreciate the way that the Lions have wrapped him and his family in warmth over the past couple years because everyone saw um their love for him on Sunday afternoon, but behind the scenes that has been consistent every step of the way. And what Dan [clears throat] Campbell said in response, I put on my Twitter, but just just I I want to share some of what he said here. He said, 'I I just want everyone to know if if you haven't grasped this yet, that Dan Miller is one of the best humans you could ever be around and you just wish that you could share that burden or take some of that burden from him because nobody deserves that. And I thought that was just the most authentically quintessentially Dan Campbell way of viewing things. Like that is the football player in him wishing that he could help a teammate in strife. Wishing wishing that he could lighten the load for someone. um even though he knows that's all but impossible. And um the outreach by Dan Campbell and Holly for for Dan Miller and Cindy Miller was so touching over the past couple years. um including um like uh Holly came to one of Dan Dan Miller sitdowns with Dan Campbell when Cindy had just been diagnosed and brought a box with uh some some like essential items in it for for any cancer patient. and she said she gave the box to Dan and said, "You don't have to open this now, but when you get home, open it with Cindy and you'll probably end up needing these things over the course of her diagnosis." title: Sam Darnold: "There Needs To Be A Sense Of Urgency To Get Better" | Seattle Seahawks
text: How's it going? >> Got you guys outside today. >> Yeah. >> Nice. Um, yeah, obviously a short week, so uh, you know, we're rolling on a Tuesday. It's, uh, it's amazing. Just another opportunity to go out there, play good football. Obviously learned a lot from from last week. You know, got to, you know, I think it's really the same thing of what I said right after the game. You know, just got to be a little bit more decisive, um, you know, out there and continue to put the ball in play, get the ball moving forward on first and second down. Sam, uh, last year coming out, you were throwing it faster than you ever thrown, uh, time to throw and you're still getting explosives. This year it's slower. What are the obviously you want to throw it more quickly. What are the factors [clears throat] that are maybe playing into that? >> Yeah, I think, you know, first of all, I got to do a better job of, you know, getting the ball out, moving on in progression, stuff like that. So, you know, um there's that and then obviously there's a lot of other factors that go into it, but for me, like I'm just I'm worried about myself and how I can, you know, continue to be as decisive as I can be on the field. >> Sam Hoop said that one of your best qualities is your ability to have a short-term memory and kind of just move on. Has that something is that something you've always had or do you develop in some way? >> Um it's not something I always had. Um, I think just some of the experiences that I've had in my life being in the NFL, college, high school, like you know, um, just things maybe not going a certain way, um, and just learning over time that there's a lot of things that are out of my control. So, just having that short-term memory and knowing that you can't change anything in the past, um, is always a good reminder as well. >> The turnovers have been kind of teamwide as well. Is it is there any worried all of it becomes something that you guys think about or, you know, they kind of come in bunches kind of thing and it's hard to come? No, you Yeah, I think for us it's uh there's there's a sense of urgency. I think that term, you know, that phrase like sense of urgency, it's been thrown around a lot the last couple days and it's true. You know, there needs to be a sense of urgency to get better and have ball security. Um, for me personally, like I'm just I'm going to continue to try to be as decisive as I can be and and go through my reads and trust what I see, trust my feet, all those things. Um, but yeah, can't have turnovers. um you know it's you got to protect the football in this league and um if you don't you'll pay. >> What's uh Brian's demeanor been like this week and what's the gist of his message to you guys offensively? >> Yeah, he's been great. Um you know, he's been the same. Nothing nothing's changed. Uh you know, for us it's just again, it's just about turning the page and and understanding that we have a really good defense we're going up against uh Thursday night and getting as prepared as we can be to face them. wanting to turn that fade. How much does the short week maybe help in that way? I'm sure you just want to get back out there and fix it right away. >> Yeah, no doubt. No doubt. I think it definitely helps. You know, getting to play a game on Thursday is always fun. So, in front of everybody, too. Um there's nothing like it. So, we'll be ready to go. >> Part of uh you know, getting early down success is a little bit more success in the run game. Uh are you seeing, you know, potential there for things to start getting a little more productive? Yeah, I think it's I mean it all kind of works hand in hand, right? Like you know for me like on on first and second pass game I got to get the ball out. Um when I get the ball out then all of a sudden defenders are thinking about what pass plays might be coming up and then all of a sudden we're running the football. Um so yeah it, you know, the run game, the pass game, it complements each other. So, um, I think if we just all continue to, you know, detail everything out and and for me just continue to to, you know, make quick decisions and and feel really good about them and and trust in my feet and all those things, um, you know, we'll we'll continue to um to see, you know, ourselves grow in the pass game and the run game. >> How do you not rush, make quick decisions without rushing? I think you talk about making quick rushes. What is that balance there? >> Yeah. Yeah, there's a great balance to it, right? It's uh it's the old, you know, John Woodenism. Uh be quick but don't hurry kind of thing. So, yeah, it's it's, you know, understanding when something might not be there. Still give it a chance because it's in the progression, but understanding when you might move on. And I think if I just continue to or if I do a better job of that moving forward, um you know, I'll like where I um where I'm going to be head forward. >> You guys are seeing more cover zero this year than you did last year. Uh, you know, it's a chance for some explosives as well. You see, if you control the the turnovers, do you see some potential for explosives to come out of it as well? >> Yeah, I think anytime you control the turnovers, like everything else gets better, you know? So, it's uh that's really the thing we're we're focused on is just taking care of the football. And I think that's that's the main thing that we're focused on, but at the same time, you know, we're just going to continue to play fast as well. Sam, what stands out about Denver's defense specifically? >> Yeah, I think first of all, they got really good players. Um, and they got a really good coaching staff over there. Vance Vance and that coaching staff do a really good job of, you know, making sure that they all, you know, they they do a lot of things in the back end. They do a lot of pressures, a lot of different coverages, but they're all on the same page. And, you know, I would assume they make it very simple for the players. So, it's uh, you know, it's a great scheme. And uh I know we're very very excited um to be able to go up against that defense and uh but yeah, again, like I said, just really good players all around and and with really good scheme and all the players are are smart players that make it come to life. >> When you have a couple weeks that don't go exactly the way you want, where do you start? Do you go back to mechanics? Do you go to film? Do you go like where do you start to to kind of get back to center? Yeah, I think I think for me it's you know it's easy to overthink things um you know when you start when you're not having as much success as you'd like. Um so I think for me it's just continuing to do what I do and you know continue to trust the process. Like I'm not you know I'm not doing anything different the week that I did you know last year the weeks prior. So um just continue to do my process. Obviously a short week makes it a little bit different. Um, but just trust the process and and understand that, you know, there's things that I got to do differently on the field, right? Um, and understand what those mistakes are and not make them again. And I think it's that simple. >> Is trusting the process easier now because of the the success you have had the last couple years. >> Yeah, I feel like I've just found a good rhythm within my process. um to your point, you know, just but again, like I I feel like I've always said this, but um going and finding that process was always a challenge. And now that I found it, it's just continuing to trust that and and you know what we do throughout the week to get ready. Anything >> else? Thanks, guys.

title: Julian Love On The Team's Mindset Heading Into Week 6: "We're Pretty Hungry" | Seattle Seahawks
text: How we doing? >> Julian, what have you found most effective when you have a short week? And I guess you're also got the altitude to deal with too. >> Yeah. Uh I know Sam Rams in uh Andre and Sammy the nutritionists have a great great plan like immediately after the game they kind of gave us a little pamphlet, little flyer sheet, you know, hydration, sleep, all those kind of things. Uh can't really do too much with the altitude. Just make sure everything else is lined up. >> How much do you feel it? And then what is it like when you're playing at altitude? >> I don't know. This is going to be a first for me. my first time playing over there. Um, so yeah, I'm excited to experience it. Uh, and yeah, hopefully I'll be ready to go. >> I I'm know you guys are probably always going to be critical on defense and lot went well in this game. Red zone still seems like you guys haven't been able to keep people out of the end zone as much. Anything that you're finding there that maybe you think you're going to turn that around soon? >> Yeah, I think just as a whole it's I mean it's a targeted focus for us. um turning some of those situations into a field goal attempt as opposed to a seven um is huge. This is kind of how we have to play complimentary football and we did not do that uh well enough on defense Sunday. Um so yeah, it's it's an area of of high importance right now. We trying to continually work at it. Um I can't tell you exactly what it looks like, but I know that it is uh it's important to us. >> Defensively, what trends have you seen in the fourth quarter of the last couple of games? Um, I'm not sure. Uh, I think each game has presented different things. Uh, and the flow of each game has been pretty different. Um, I think as a team, we just got to finish games. We have to start fast. You know, always that situation where you try to play well, then just finish games. Um, put ourselves in position uh on Sunday, but it's just too many too many mistakes on our part. And so, that's we're we're not playing clean enough ball. What is kind of the the psyche of the team right now, do you feel like? >> I think we're we're pretty hungry. Um, you know, there's a lot to correct on. There's a lot to to improve. I think everyone pretty much on that field has a play or two that they're like, I wish I had that one back. And that's never great. Uh, it's never great when, you know, everyone. So, I can't, you know, we can't say it's one person. I think all of us are looking inward. Um, and just correcting that, just be sharpening up that one play. Uh, we're a good team. we know we can be uh a great team. Um and it's going to take those those one-offs to to to go away. >> On that front, Julian, like >> you played in the two losses, you've still been right there in the game. So, does that make it that much more frustrating that that that extra little bit hasn't been there so far in those couple? >> Yeah, 100%. Um but I mean, I don't know if you guys caught the vibe after the uh the uh the Chargers game. It's like, okay, we win that game, but like things just we we were frustrated because things just aren't are being played cleanly. Um I think it goes into the process. That's kind of how we attack things. It's like, okay, the final result is going to be the final result. Like we obviously try to win games, but like how do how did it look? Um what went into the game? And so there's so many corrections we could be making um guys got to play better uh situationally um individually. And so I think uh all the guys inside are are fired up, ready to turn that over. >> Yeah. What you got? >> When you're when you're chasing a clean game, like you said, h how close do you feel like you are to to turning a corner and to being able to have a performance even in a win that you feel good about? >> Yeah, I think it's really close. I feel like we go into each game very confident the process, the week, the the reps, the practice, everybody's doing their job. Everybody's doing a good job. No one like cutting corners at all. says on Sunday when it's time to execute, we have to execute. We have to make our reads. We have to make our checks. We have to perform whatever play is out there for the time. And so I think offense, defense, special teams, we just we're still we're still we're close, but obviously it's not close enough. >> How important is it for this defense to play decisiveness? What do you think is kind of, you know, not quite there yet for that to happen? >> I think we just got to get off the field. I think we have a few third downs back. I think obviously we talked about red zone. Um, that's kind of a a choice like, okay, no matter how they got here, um, could be a turnover, could be a drive, whatever. Let's make let's make the choice to force a force a kick. Um, it's a could be a four-point swing, could be huge for our our team when they're pinned, keeping them pinned. So, it gives our offense a short field. Just all those little things. So, making the choice each each play to just lock in and get the job done. >> When you take a look at Denver this week, they made a change with their play caller just a week ago. you know what Shawn Payeyton brings, but how does that change game prep when you have two different play callers this year? >> Uh it's it's definitely interesting. I think uh I mean you want all the tape in the world consistently, you know, the most recent tape on who you ever you have and so it switches things up. U you kind of go got to go back into the archives a little bit. Um but the players are still the players. Um we kind of know uh it's a talented group, a talented team, a high energy group. Um and we're going to have to bring it. Uh, we know or I've heard that Denver is is a great atmosphere and so I'm excited to see what it's like. I'm excited to compete with the guys. >> You guys didn't give up any plays over 19 yards the first couple games, but explosive plays have kind of trickled in the last few games. Uh, what are you noticing there? >> Uh, just oneoffs. Um, I think yeah, challenging uh at the point of catch uh at the point of contact um is a high priority for us right now >> with the Thursday night games. Like aside from just the physical challenge of playing 4 days after playing, what's it like playing with like I imagine you guys aren't going to have anything close to a normal practice this week. What's it like playing without really >> your typical practice? >> It's weird. Um probably early in my career I I wasn't sure how to feel about it. Um but I think the ball player in you is just like especially after like a loss, you're like, "All right, let's just line up again." Like it's the best case scenario. It's like, okay, this is no thinking, just doing. Go out there Thursday, uh, and try to win a game. Um, and so it is a little bit of that. Obviously, you it's more walkthroughs. It's more, you know, intentional meeting times, making sure you're trying to get looks and trying to get reps probably done at full speed. Um, but end of the day, it's like line the ball up and let's play. And so, that's kind of the the freedom of a Thursday night game, even though the body is still, you know, getting right. Going back to the things that you guys wanted to improve on, I think last week you guys had a players only meeting about defensive penalties. This past game you guys had, I believe just one defensive penalty. Do you guys have conversations about that? Like, hey, look, when we put our mind to something, we can enact change. >> Yeah, that's exactly how we feel in the building. It's like each each week there's been things um obviously the charge game was was penalties. This game we have a lot of things to to address. Uh we got to win the turnover battle. Um, and yeah, guys, it was kind of like just just lead it on. It's not really like a um a moment of crisis type of like like player only meeting. It's really just like, hey, let's let's talk about it. Like we're not going to shy away from things. Even though we could be, you know, five and0 right now, we're still going to talk through things as players, as teammates, as friends. Um, and so yeah, some of those conversations we already had this week, it's like, okay, what can we improve on? How can we, you know, breathe life into each other? How can we show love? how can we also hold each other accountable? Um, and everybody to a man is grown in here and so they uh, you know, they take the onus on themselves and so that's kind of the cool part of those players only moments. Um, it might not be like a formal meeting. It might just be a general conversation. Um, but it's it's constant with us. >> You mentioned you said you're a good team, not a great team, but you can be off to a similar start last year. Then you guys obviously got a lot. I know it's new season looking back, but is there value for the guys who've been around like, hey, we're capable of making this shift in season? >> Yeah, for sure. I think, you know, the grand scheme of things, you want to continually build and continue to play your best brand of football. Right now, we're not playing our best brand of football. Just straight up and down. I mean, you guys see it. Um, but it's out there. It's obtainable. I've been a part of some groups in previous life that you feel like you played a pretty clean game and you still lose by two scores. And so it's it's empowering to know it's like if we're just on our stuff, if we're on the details, we're playing together. Yeah, we can make things happen. It's obviously it's proven uh you know, in the past. Um but we still have to go through that. That that's a callous thing we have to build this year. Um you know, the mountain it's a new mountain as we've talked about and so adversity has it's showing itself. So how are we going to respond? >> What did you think of Okatada first game of the season? Oh, >> he put lights out. Um, I thought, you know, the hardest thing about coming back, trust me, is like just trusting your body, just like kind of getting out of your head and just letting the game come to you. And so I thought he made some great tackles out there. Like he his his presence was felt in a physical way. Um, when he's out there, I think everyone is a little calmer um just because he is very on point with his communication and his details. Um, and so I'm really happy for for, you know, his his coming out party this year. I think he's been excited to show what he has as a full year starter. >> Good. >> Yeah. Thank you. Appreciate it.

title: Cooper Kupp: "My Belief In This Team And The Guys Is So Great" | Seattle Seahawks
text: Cooper, how was the uh practice? And you guys already, you know, got day away from a game. So, how'd you guys attack the the last couple practices you've had? >> The last couple practices we've had since the game? >> Uh, yeah. No, we've I we've had a we've had a workout. We were in here for one day. Um, just been going to watch the film, get a workout in. Um, coach's game plan, things like that. So, we'll really uh get into a lot of the game plan specific stuff uh today. And um but yeah, just it's good being back here with the guys. I mean, I think there's that, you know, there's that that uneasy feeling um in the facility right now of just being, you know, coming off of a loss, a game that we feel like we should have won and just didn't do well enough, especially offensively. Like there's there's a frustration there. Um but also that healthy man um chomping at the opportunity to go out there and play another another football game here in a couple days. So, um there's excitement there and um yeah, looking forward to to getting after things. You mentioned it felt like a game you should have won lost you should have won. Going back like early last season the only three games you lost and you had 11 turnovers. Is that more frustrating or is there a sense it's almost like okay we're we're the only thing that beats up to themselves? >> Yeah. Yeah. I mean I think there is that there's I mean if you want to grab any positive out of it it's that um you know you don't most times you turn the ball over that many times you you are not in a position to to win the game at the end of it. and u we've battled and found a way to to be in that position and so you know is that um there is that as a positive but it is man getting out out of your own way and not putting our defense in tough positions um yeah we we just have to be better there >> and there has been a growth with Brian Flory offensive coordinator what's the logical next step that the offense takes now after a few weeks >> yeah just putting it all together like we've we have flashes and moments of um of efficiency moments of explosive ess um and and moments of just we're playing really good football. And then we also have moments where it's just not good enough and there's mistakes and there's going backwards and there's, you know, self-inflicted wounds and um it's finding ways to eliminate those and keep things moving forward, keep the ball moving forward. Um you know, it's it's our own stuff. It's our own stuff right now and we we just have to be better there. >> Did did watching the film of it change your mind at all on the last play and whether you might have got that? There's been a lot of debate about whether you did or didn't. >> Yeah, I mean I don't know. I mean, like I said, at the moment I thought I had gotten it. The refs said it was not. And that's just like you live with that. You live with the fact that that's I mean, you you live and die by those decisions. And um this is a game of the NFL is, you know, win loss on razor thin margins. And if you're going to put yourself in a position to have the game decided by that, then it's it's really on us. You know, we should never been in that spot to begin with. Um not not much reason to put any energy into it. Um it's been decided and um shall move on. Last year, uh, first part of the season, you guys were getting rid of the ball really quickly and throwing the ball downfield, pretty explosive. This year, it's taking a little longer to get rid of the ball and the plays aren't as much down the field. What do you think needs to change to help Sam and the offense be a little bit more on time uh, and while keeping the explosive aspect? >> Yeah, you know, um, there's probably a lot to unpack there. Um, you know, you can look at there's a lot of different things going on in terms of, you know, the games that you're in, how those games are playing out, what plays are being activated based on the circumstances of the game. Um, and, uh, you know, and the defenses that we're seeing. So, um, you know, there's a lot there and, um, I'm honestly would probably end up saying more than I should if I I you know, really get into it. But, um, you know, there's there's a lot there that as an offense we can do. We all have, like, like I've said before, we we all have a hand, you know, in the ball coming out. And um, you know, that's finding ways to um turn short passes into explosives, finding ways to distribute the field quickly, get to the right spots, identify what the defense is doing, um, and get to the places we're supposed to so that Sam can get rid of the ball. It's being having great eye discipline, um, understanding where you are in the progression. Um, you know, there's so much that's a part of that. um and we all play a role in it and we're all going to get get much better and make sure that um those things do come alive where the ball is getting out, but we're also able to uh be efficient and keep uh explosives um going. >> You have a unique perspective being sometimes in the quarterback room in some of those meetings and in the receiver room. How are those conversations the same? How are they different right now >> uh between the receiver room and the QB room? Yeah. Well, I mean, I think there's that, you know, the great thing is that everyone's very critical of themselves in their respective rooms, right? Like, you know, you're not in the quarterback room hearing all the things the receiver is supposed to do, but you're not in the receiver room hearing all the things the quarterback should be doing, right? It's like the QB room, it's what can the QB do better. Um, I'm I'm get to see where I can also make the mental note of like, hey, we can also be better in these situations as well. Um, but in the wide receiver room, it's like, hey, how can we what how can we handle what we handle and be in the right spots? How do we u make sure that we're doing our job to the best of our ability? And um you know that's what that's that's why my belief in this team and the guys is is so great is because everyone is living that same life. You know it's how critical can you be in your room? How much better can we be by position? Um and you know the the the view is all inward and um you know that's why uh I'm excited about going out there today and and having a great great practice and um moving forward towards Denver. Have you have you learned any tricks to handling the Thursday kind of the quick turnaround to Thursday games and all your years doing this? >> Yeah, there there's no real tricks to it. You just decide that you're going to you just tell your body like you just you have no choice but to be ready by Thursday and um it finds a way to get >> With the way Sam's kind of his mental makeup, his approach, how does that help him, you know, if he is coming off a game where things are going his way? >> Yeah, I mean it's an elite trait of his to stay steady be able to go through the highs and lows of of life of football of of a play. Um and it's just uh his steadiness is a is an incredible trait and um it's a great thing for us as an offense knowing that like man there's he knows that we have a you know supreme belief in him um when he steps in the huddle it's a next play mindset next good ball and um as the guy that's coming into the huddle even whatever's happened before he's coming with great energy and excitement for be able to go out there and play efficient ball for that next drive and so um you know that's what you need you can't have uh you can't have anyone lingering can't have anyone holding back because you can feel that as you step up to line when someone's still stuck on the play that happened before. Um, and you know, we've done a great job moving forward from those things and I just have to be able to do that consistently. >> What's it like playing in the altitude? How much do you feel it? >> I think you I mean you you feel a little bit maybe in a little bit in pregame. You'll feel it the first couple drives, but then it's like, hey, look, you got to have a little mental fortitude and understand that, you know, this is what it is. And um you got to find a way to to overcome that stuff. And um you know there's going to be a little bit of excitement, a little bit of grit um that you can kind of tap into and just understand, hey, this is this is football at Mile High. This is what it's going to be. And I'm sure that place is going to be rocking and be a great environment. Um, you know, and and you know, there's a lot that goes into it, you know, and so, um, I'm not sure why that why it is, but I mean, it could it's probably a mixture of a lot of different things. And so, um, so yeah, it's definitely something. Um, and, uh, you know, we just have to be a good job, do a good job offensively of being able to counter that thing. >> Anything else, guys? >> Awesome. Thank you guys. Sheep.
