title: Sean Mannion on Loss to Jacksonville Jaguars
text: Would you would you like to see Jaylen run more? >> You know, I think uh we're always looking for ways to integrate him into the run game. Some of it's dependent on the opponent and um you know, the fronts are giving us, the looks you're getting, but um like I've said here before, it's it's a unique trait that he has that makes him dangerous. Some of them are designed, some of them are kind of the offset plays. Um I think he's had a good feel for that in terms of when to take off and run. you know, he had some big plays early in the year, first few weeks of of using his legs in the pass game, kind of those off schedule scrambles. Um, so there's a place for both of them. Um, I think he's found a nice balance of that. >> Was there something about this game where it wasn't a bigger part of the plan? >> No, I think, uh, you know, each week presents a different challenge, you know, um, and we're going to do whatever we can each week to go and win the game. We felt like this week, um, you know, we were a little bit more passoriented. Um, some of that is is in intentional, some of it's just how the game plays out and the adjustments you're making in game, but um, you know, we want to be an offense that is balanced and can attack you in the run game and the pass game and then kind of within the game, within the week, the opponent you're facing, um, you know, your personnel. Um, there can be little tweaks along the way that lead to a different, you know, kind of end result in terms of your run pass bound. >> Did you have a calf injury limited in that? >> I didn't I didn't think so. you know, he uh I thought he was ready to play and and performed well. >> How do you think uh Jake Mers, Willie, and Markeel held up kind of in their first or I guess Markeel second, but overall that young offensive line? >> Yeah, you know, I thought they got their feet underneath them. You know, there was a couple plays early on where, you know, like anyone um you know, I've been in their shoes, your your first NFL action, um you know, there's a lot of, you know, emotion, you know, positively that goes into kind of your first taste of that. Um, but I thought really as the game went on, they got their feet underneath them. They communicated well. I mean, they played hard. That's one thing, you know, and I say it every week, but this group really, really plays hard. But, you know, especially Willie, Jake, Markeel, those young guys, you can just see the the uh, you know, ferocity they're playing with out there. That's what you appreciate about them. And these are three young players that we have a ton of confidence in. You know, they're talented. Um, you know, they're getting their first taste of real action. I think they're going to keep getting better. Um, we feel good about the depth of this group, you know, while we're kind of weathering the storm through some of these injuries. When >> the second half struggles, Sean, we talked about it uh in the past. Are when you look at it, are any themes developing from your standpoint of what needs to be adjusted? >> Yeah, you know, we're we're looking at that hard each and every week. Um, you know, as a as a staff, you know, um, how to find our rhythm, find our footing in the second half. I thought we did a better job and there were some close calls I think could have really it was more about finishing those drives. I think we came out in the second half had some third down conversions had a close call on on the deep shot to Wix. Um you know I think there was some um you know some some chances there that we just didn't quite capitalize on. But ultimately as a staff I I I'm I'm look looking every week to put ourselves in the best position possible kind of leaving halftime um to extend those drives. I think we're closer. You know, I know the result hasn't been um what we want or or what we what we hold ourselves to as an offense, but um I felt like we were getting closer in those sec in the second half. We really just have to finish some of those drives. >> Has the heavy use of of the condensed formations contributed to the amount of unblocked rushers or the pressure you've seen? >> Um it's a balance, I think. Um, you know, there's certain things just having lived in kind of this system for a while that teams may try to do against it with, um, condensed splits and, you know, um, different things like that, how you're aligned. There are some things that are thematically happening throughout the league at large um, against that. Um, and then some of it is just execution, you know, for us as coaches, making sure we're doing the best job possible to to really teach the guys and train the guys for what those looks can be. um because ultimately it's our job as coaches to to to detail all that up um to put them in the in the best position to succeed as possible. But certainly, you know, different teams attack you in different ways. Um you know, and some of it's specific to us, some of it's specific to kind of familiar schemes, and some of it are just leaguewide trends that you see around the league. You know, um everyone's watching so much tape um that people get ideas from everywhere. on the second down throw to Mai Lemon before the field goal on the out pattern when he didn't go out of bounds. Was was he coached to to stay in bounds? >> Our our focus there was really just to advance the ball. They were in a cover zero look. Um with that comes, you know, some leverage issues where you're inside. Um so we wanted the primary focus there was advance the ball to do our best to help the kick. Um you know, and then get us into the best play possible to do so and avoid a negative play. So that was the the outcome we had there. Obviously he was caught, you know, caught on the outbreak right by the sideline kind of got pushed out. Um but our our primary focus with the call and with the execution of it was to advance the ball. Um you know with the look that's what that's what ended up happening where we had an outbreak and um ends up getting pushed out. >> You think that he couldn't have done anything to to >> I felt like it was a bang bang play right on the sideline. Again we were focused um on how do we help our how how do we help the kick? Um because that was the primary primary focus what was happening. >> Was he Can I just ask one more? Is he the first like read on that on that play? >> Uh yes. >> Sean, uh Jaylen's a career 65% passer. He's at like 57 change this year. What do you think that's a product of? >> You know, I I don't think it's any one thing. I think across the board, right, offensively, we want to keep pushing to be better. Um and that's in all phases. That's run game, pass game. Um that's us putting together the best plan possible each week. Um you know, I think he is is a naturally very accurate guy. Um, you know, so I'm confident that that those numbers will will continue to improve. His comfort level grows each and every week. Um, you know, getting these live game reps week after week after week. Um, he's going to grow more and more comfortable. And, you know, I think the good thing is he's he's been making good decisions with the ball. You know, obviously had an uptick in our pass attempts last game and and uh, you know, I thought he he made good decisions with with where the ball was supposed to go and I'm confident because he is a naturally accurate passer that those numbers will rise. terms of setting protections, I believe you said before sometimes it could be the center, sometimes the quarterback depending on the the play or the scheme. Are are you shifting that more towards Jaylen given the turnover that you've had at the center position? >> You know, I think it's always um like I said, not to get into the details of the scheme. I think it depends on the protection scheme in terms of what kind of each um kind of different part of the protection unit controls in terms of the center or the quarterback. Um, without getting into that, I think the beauty of it is, you know, with the turnover at the center position, they're all very, very capable of handling that. Um, so I guess a short answer would be, um, even with the changes up front, we've kind of, uh, kept the continuity of who's in charge of what in terms of the protection system. >> What were some of the issues with the run game, the struggles in the run game uh, this past game? And then is there any consideration maybe to using Carson Steel in a fullback role to kind of lead block into a hole? >> Yeah, I'll uh I'll talk about both those things. So, you know, again, I think you go into each game thinking how are we going to win? Um you know, different teams present different challenges in terms of their personnel, in terms of their alignments. Um, so you know, that plays a part in kind of the number of attempts and and you're you're kind of always adjusting in terms of what you think will help us move the ball in the next series in terms of how you're calling it in terms of run and pass. I feel confident this group's going to be able to move the ball. We had some nice um runs earlier on in the in the uh you know, in the run game. Um we just need to keep sustaining that and then honestly some of it's not necessarily a negative. You feel better about some of the other calls you have on the sheet um and you get to those. Um, getting to Carson, you know, he did a phenomenal job in the preseason. He's wearing a ton of different hats with us out on the practice field. Um, especially as we're kind of weathering the storm through some of these injuries. Um, he's a versatile player, um, who can do a lot of nice things for us. We're looking to use all of our guys in every way possible. So, that's certainly something we're considering. >> So, going back to Mai's uh, the thro Mai, I understand that the goal is to advance the ball. Um but but why I guess and I understand he was pushed out of bounds but but why was it best in that situation for him to run an outre an outbreaking route just in general? >> Yeah, not to get too far into the weeds of of the scheme, but you know in cover zero leaguewide, you know, typically there you're going to be fighting a battle of inside leverage. Um so sometimes again the most productive play to try to advance the ball means running away from that inside leverage. Now different teams attack you different ways. Um but again, our primary focus in that moment was uh advancing the ball for the kick. Um when you're fighting hard inside leverage, the best way to do that typically is an outbreaker. Um so that's kind of how that that came to happen. >> When you're calling plays on when there's a lot of game management involved for Nick and the clock, how does that how does that dynamic work? >> It's been smooth. Um you know, we've had a bunch of them honestly come up organically in practice. Um, I think that's something that obviously is a focal point for Nick. We practice we practice it like crazy where we'll just call a two-minute drive and and let it play out. And it's not a scripted scenario, but it's me standing back there with the walkie-talkie. I'm with Nick exactly how it would be on game day where we're monitoring the clock, we're monitoring our timeout situation, advancing the ball, you know, do we need a field goal? Do we need a touchdown? So, we've gotten a lot of good bank reps of that. There's been ones that have come up earlier in the year, you know, we had a two-minute drive against Tennessee. Um, you know, where we go right down to the wire, you know, we almost had, you know, some really kind of unique situational circumstances come up where we have a review. Um, is he inbounds, out of bounds? So, I think throughout all of that, um, to get back to original question, I think the communication has been great with me and Nick. Um, the people up in the box, we're talking through the situations, we're monitoring the clock. Um, that communication's been smooth. as the guy in charge of the the game management, is he telling you what type of plays to run? >> We talk through all those scenarios um throughout the week, we have, you know, a ton of parameters and contingencies. Um so it's it's not necessarily play type. We're talking about the different scenarios and then, you know, as you can tell, there's a lot of different variables. Um but we map those out really throughout the week in terms of what we want to do. So in the moment it's not discussion as m uh in terms of the specific play. It's more going to the what kind of um group of parameters do does our play uh our call sheet um call for in that in that setting. I guess we we map these out ahead of time. >> The touch push. >> Yeah, it was something that was on the call sheet. Um you know, we had the short yardage look. Each team attacks short yardage differently. Um, you know, I think the other thing is is we felt like we could get ourselves into an optimum look um in short yardage by staying in the gun. Um, you know, we had a downhill run play. You know, we need to execute it better. We need to, you know, you know, I have the utmost confidence with whomever is in there. Um, that they're going to be able to execute a short yardage run, a short yardage pass, a tush push. Um, if I didn't have confidence, it wouldn't end up on the sheet. But, um, the tush push is absolutely still a part of what we believe in. Um we felt like in that uh short yardage situation um with you know the the the yardage to gain you know um it being a full yard there and then with the characteristics of their defense uh we felt like the best play possible was um an inside zone from the gun I guess the the day-to-day grind. How's the job going so far? How are you adjusting to it? How is it it different from what you might have expected? Yeah, it's been uh you know, again, I know we're fighting tooth and nail every day. Um to get the results that I know we can get. Um the results I know we want. Um you know, the thing with the work the work part of it is is it it really is that's the part you love. You love coming in here every day, you know, working your tail off with your staff, with your players. Um you know, working as a unit to try to achieve the best result possible. I know we're still fighting for for what we want that to look like. Um, but my enthusiasm, my enjoyment with that process has not waned in the slightest. Um, it's been a blast. You know, there's new challenges every day, whether it be uh managing injuries or whether it be managing, you know, a practice plan or or, you know, traveling overseas. How does that adjust our our offensive meeting schedule? But that that honestly is the enjoyable part. That's that's why you love getting into coaching is you get to work with, you know, other great coaches, get to work with a phenomenal group of players um that work their butt off. Um they're coachable, they want to win, they want to get better. Um so yeah, it's uh it's a new challenge every day in this role. Um but it's everything I hoped it would be and it's been it's been a blast. And you know, I am really confident that if we keep attacking the day with the right, you know, attacking each day with the right mindset, with you know, high level of enthusiasm, um with just a will to just get better by bit, day by day, we are going to get the the results that that we're after. the primary stat that you're looking at, Sean, that sort of represents the area that needs the most improvement for you guys to get to where you want to get to? >> Yeah, that's a great question. You know, it's hard to boil it down to just one. Um, you know, there's a lot of different metrics you can look at. Um, and I think some of it, you know, you attack a different thing each week. You know, early on, first, you know, week one or two, you know, we were struggling to stay on schedule. So, first and second down efficiency was something that was a major focal point. Um, you know, then, you know, obviously a couple weeks, couple weeks ago, you know, we we weren't as good as we wanted to be on third down. So then, you know, third down conversion percentage, you know, that's a metric we want to attack. So, um, it can be a little bit of a of a of a moving target. You obviously want to be good in as many different areas as you can be. Um, but your primary focus, you know, I'd say it it shifts sometimes from one to the next cuz there's a lot of different things that you can look at, whether it be explosive play rate, efficiency, um, third down percentage, so on and so forth. Um, you know, I think we've done a good job of addressing things as they've, you know, as we've seen them and as we, you know, we got better at first and second down efficiency. We were better on third down last week than we were the week before. Um, again, I think ultimately it all goes back to can we make incremental improvements um with our fundamentals um offensively, what with what we're doing schematically and I think all of those metrics will rise. >> When it comes to when it comes to managing injuries, I mean, obviously you don't have Saquon, you don't have Devonte. >> How difficult is it to like kind of, you know, design plays or, you know, run the offense without having those two guys in there? Yeah, I think you again it all goes back to putting um all of your players in what you feel is the best position for them to be successful. Um you know, Saquon is a unique talent. There's there that's it's indisputable, right? So there's things that he can do that there's a very very very short list uh of people on the planet that can do. Um the beauty of it is I do feel really confident in our depth. Um you know, Tank, you know, going going out due to injury, you know, but he's a really really quality backup running back in this league. So, um, there may be some things that change when Saquon goes out and tank goes in, but the nice thing is with the depth that we have at that position, just as an example, it's not as many as you might you might expect, um, because of the depth of our roster, the confidence we have in those guys. Um, so there's tweaks here and there that that come up with different injuries, you know, whether it be at the running back position, receiver position, O line. Um, but in in large, the confidence of that we have in our group makes it where that's easier to manage than you you may think. >> All right. Exactly.

When you think about how well the Steelers have worked offensively the last three weeks, remember that was the question the first two weeks the Steelers had started as one of the worst offenses not just of the last five years, but of the last 10 years for the first two games. Points per game, success rate, EPA per play, rush success rate. Um just big time stuff from the Steelers. They have looked like a top 10 offense over the last three weeks.
